chunks: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the skins of al-Khazz, so he said: 'It is that al-Khazz which we wear.' So I said: 'May I be your sacrifice! That is the fur?' He said: 'When its fur is permissible, its skin is permissible.'

key_terms.الخز: Al-Khazz — a semi-aquatic animal (otter or mink); also refers to a type of fabric woven from its hair/wool
key_terms.جلود: Plural of jild (skin/hide); here referring to the tanned skin used for clothing or footwear
key_terms.حل: To be permissible/lawful; from the root ح-ل-ل (halal)
key_terms.وبر: Fur/wool/soft hair, especially from camelids or semi-aquatic animals; the fine underfur

ai.seo_question: Is wearing al-Khazz (otter/mink) skin permissible in Islam according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) was asked about the permissibility of wearing skins from al-Khazz (a semi-aquatic animal, likely otter or mink). The Imam first confirmed that al-Khazz is worn by the Imams themselves, and when clarification was sought about whether this referred to its fur, he established a general legal principle: if the fur of an animal is permissible, then its skin/hide is equally permissible. This ruling addresses a common jurisprudential question about the status of animal by-products in Shia fiqh.
